basic_identification.full_title: Wrought Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Bars, Rods, Tubes, Sections, Plates and Sheets for Electrical Applications — Specification (Second Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering / Light Metals and Their Alloys (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Light Metals and Their Alloys Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards) [1]

sectional_committee.name: Light Metals and Their Alloys Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for wrought aluminium and aluminium alloy bars, rods, tubes, sections, plates, and sheets for electrical applications (such as busbars, tubular conductors, and terminal fittings), prescribing their chemical composition, mechanical properties, and electrical resistivity/conductivity limits. It applies to extruded products of 6 mm diameter and above, sections of 3 mm thickness and above, and rolled plates/sheets.

amendment_slips.description: Substitutes 'Percent Elongation on 5.65√So gauge length' for 'Percent Elongation on 50 mm Gauge Length' in Table 2, Column 5.

Replaces legacy references for chemical analysis (IS 504) with the updated multi-part standards IS 504 (Parts 1 to 12) : 2002 and IS 504 (Parts 13 to 16) : 2013 [1, 2]. It also replaces legacy references for tensile testing (IS 1608) with the modernized IS 1608 (Part 1) / ISO 6892-1 [2].

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order' (Aluminium QCO) issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all wrought aluminium and aluminium alloy products for electrical applications manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 5082 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified electrical-grade aluminium bars, rods, or tubes is a statutory offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial alloy conductors.

requirements.detail: Every package or bundle of electrical-grade aluminium products must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to certify compliance.
The standard covers two primary chemical designations designed for electrical applications: a) Grade 19501 (Electrolytic Grade / EC); b) Grade 63401 (Al-Mg-Si Alloy Grade / E91E).

The products are supplied in designated tempers based on material type: a) Grade 19501: Supplied in 'M' (fully annealed), 'H1', or 'H2' tempers; b) Grade 63401: Supplied in 'W' (solution heat-treated) or 'WP' (precipitation-hardened/artificial aging) tempers (WP range 1 and WP range 2).
The nominal physical densities used for dimensional conversions and calculations are: a) Grade 19501: 2.705 g/cm³; b) Grade 63401: 2.700 g/cm³.

The high-purity composition of Grade 19501 requires: Aluminium (minimum 99.50 percent by mass), Copper (maximum 0.04 percent), Iron (maximum 0.35 percent), Silicon (maximum 0.15 percent), and Titanium (maximum 0.02 percent).

The alloyed composition of Grade 63401 requires: Silicon (0.3 to 0.70 percent by mass), Magnesium (0.4 to 0.90 percent), Iron (maximum 0.50 percent), Copper (maximum 0.05 percent), Manganese (maximum 0.03 percent), and Aluminium (Remainder).

Grade 19501 must demonstrate exceptional electrical performance: maximum electrical resistivity at 20°C is strictly limited to 0.0287 Ω·mm²/m (equivalent to a minimum electrical conductivity of 60.0 percent IACS).

Grade 63401 in WP Range-2 temper (commonly used for high-current bus ducts and switchgear panels) must satisfy a maximum electrical resistivity at 20°C of 0.0321 Ω·mm²/m (equivalent to an electrical conductivity range of 0.0305 to 0.0321 Ω·mm²/m).
Grade 63401 in WP Range-1 temper must satisfy a maximum electrical resistivity at 20°C of 0.0325 Ω·mm²/m.
Finished annealed Grade 19501 (M) products must demonstrate: a) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 60 MPa; b) Elongation: minimum 25 percent.

Finished artificially aged Grade 63401 (WP Range-2) products must demonstrate: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 170 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 200 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 10 percent over 5.65√So gauge length.

Bars, sheets, and plates must undergo bend testing: specimens must be bent through an angle of 90 degrees or 180 degrees (depending on thickness) around a mandrel of specified radius without showing any visual signs of cracking or surface tearing.

The finished products must be clean, smooth, straight, of uniform quality, and free from cracks, voids, laminations, seams, slivers, folds, or non-metallic inclusions that would compromise mechanical or electrical reliability.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 5082 : 1998 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification regulating wrought aluminium and aluminium alloy products (such as bars, rods, tubes, sections, plates, and sheets) designed specifically for electrical applications, including power distribution bus ducts, switchgear panels, and terminal fittings. Under India's statutory national Aluminium Quality Control Order (QCO), all such electrical-grade aluminium conductors must conform to this standard and carry the Bureau of Indian Standards Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It specifies two major alloys: Grade 19501 (high-purity electrolytic aluminium with a minimum conductivity of 60.0% IACS) and Grade 63401 (an Al-Mg-Si structural alloy). It mandates rigorous mechanical and physical testing—including tensile, bend, and high-precision electrical resistivity measurements—and incorporates Amendment No. 3 (March 2022) to align all testing protocols with advanced chemical analysis (IS 504 parts) and mechanical tension (IS 1608 / ISO 6892-1) testing frameworks [1, 2].
